questions.knowledge_point: Writing a Triple Integral as a Repeated Integral
questions.problem:
Express the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}(x+2y)^{2}\,\,\text{d}V
$$

over the box

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le 3}
$$

as a repeated integral of the form 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{e}^{f}…\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Given the limits for $x,y,$ and $z,$ we can express our triple integral as a repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+2y)^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2y)^{2}\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy
$$

Given that the triple integral above is considered over the rectangular box

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 3,\,1\le y\le 4,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2},
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy.
$$

Therefore, $a+b=1+4=5.$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{y{e}^{z}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\le x\le \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{ln}⁡5}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{y{e}^{z}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}/4}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{y{e}^{z}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}]\times [0,1]\times [0,\operatorname{ln}⁡5]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}/4}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{y{e}^{z}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}/4}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot y\cdot {e}^{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}/4}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}/4}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z & ={[-\frac{1}{x}]}_{\sqrt{2}/4}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\cdot [{e}^{z}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\  & =(-\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{2})\cdot (\frac{1}{2}-0)\cdot (5-1) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot 4 \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{{y}^{2}(z-1)}{x}\,\text{d}V,\,
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le 2,\,1\le z\le 3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{{y}^{2}(z-1)}{x}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{y}^{2}(z-1)}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[1,e]\times [0,2]\times [1,3]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{y}^{2}(z-1)}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\cdot {y}^{2}\cdot (z-1)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{3}(z-1)\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{3}(z-1)\,\text{d}z & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{1}^{e}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}-z]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (\frac{8}{3}-0)\cdot (\frac{9}{2}-3-\frac{1}{2}+1) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{8}{3}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{16}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{{e}^{z+y}}{x}\,\text{d}V,\,
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{{e}^{z+y}}{x}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{e}^{z+y}}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[1,e]\times [0,\operatorname{ln}⁡3]\times [0,\operatorname{ln}⁡2]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{e}^{z+y}}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{e}^{z}\cdot {e}^{y}}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z & ={[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]}_{1}^{e}\cdot {[{e}^{y}]}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {[{e}^{z}]}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =1\cdot (3-1)\cdot (2-1) \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V,\,
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \pi ,\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{1}{2}\le z\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,\pi ]\times [0,\frac{\pi }{2}]\times [\frac{1}{2},1]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y\cdot \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi }\cdot [\operatorname{sin}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2}\cdot {[-\frac{1}{z}]}_{1/2}^{1} \\  & =(1+1)\cdot (1-0)\cdot (-1+2) \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,-1\le y\le 1,\,1\le z\le e}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,\operatorname{ln}⁡3]\times [-1,1]\times [1,e]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z & =[{e}^{x}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot [y]_{-1}^{1}\cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡z]_{1}^{e} \\  & =(3-1)\cdot (1-(-1))\cdot (1-0) \\  & =2\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}z{e}^{x}+2y\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,-1\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}z{e}^{x}+2y\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}z{e}^{x}+2y\,dx\,dz\,dy
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}z{e}^{x}+2y\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3}z{e}^{x}+2y\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z{e}^{x}+2xy]_{x=0}^{x=3}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}z({e}^{3}-1)+2(3-0)y\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{3}-1)z+6y\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{3}-1)z+6y\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{3}-1)z+6y\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{2}\,{z}^{2}+6yz]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{2}(1-0)+6y(1-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{2}+6y\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{2}+6y\,dy & ={[\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{2}\,y+3{y}^{2}]}_{y=-1}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{2}(1-(-1))+3(1-1) \\  & ={e}^{3}-1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \pi ,\,0\le z\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dx\,dy\,dz
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{1}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dx]dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+xz]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}(1-0)\operatorname{cos}⁡y+(1-0)z\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dy\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+z\,dy]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+yz]}_{y=0}^{y=\pi }\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}(0-0)+(\pi -0)z\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\pi z\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\pi z\,dz & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}z\,dz \\  & =\pi {[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}(x-y){e}^{z}\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 0,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\le z\le 2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}(x-y){e}^{z}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{2}(x-y){e}^{z}\,dz\,dx\,dy
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{2}(x-y){e}^{z}\,dz\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{2}(x-y){e}^{z}\,dz]dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}[(x-y){e}^{z}]_{z=\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{z=2}\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)({e}^{2}-2)\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)({e}^{2}-2)\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)({e}^{2}-2)\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[({e}^{2}-2){\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({e}^{2}-2){[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-xy]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({e}^{2}-2)[\frac{1}{2}(1-0)-(1-0)y]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({e}^{2}-2)(\frac{1}{2}-y)dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}({e}^{2}-2)(\frac{1}{2}-y)dy & =({e}^{2}-2){\int }_{-1}^{0}\frac{1}{2}-y\,dy \\  & =({e}^{2}-2){[\frac{1}{2}y-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=-1}^{y=0} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-2}{2}(0-(-1)+1) \\  & ={e}^{2}-2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}5x-3y\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2,\,-1\le z\le 0}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}5x-3y\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{2}5x-3y\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{2}5x-3y\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}[{\int }_{0}^{2}5x-3y\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{[5xy-\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}5x(2-0)-\frac{3}{2}(4-0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}10x-6\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}10x-6\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-1}^{0}10x-6\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(10x-6)z]_{z=-1}^{z=0}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(10x-6)(0-(-1))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}10x-6\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}10x-6\,dx & =[5{x}^{2}-6x]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =5(1-0)-6(1-0) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{y}^{2}\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \pi ,\,0\le y\le 1,\,-1\le z\le 2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}z\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }z\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{y}^{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }z\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{y}^{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }z\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{y}^{2}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}[-z\operatorname{cos}⁡x+x{y}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=\pi }\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}-z(-1-1)+{y}^{2}(\pi -0)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}2z+\pi {y}^{2}\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}2z+\pi {y}^{2}\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-1}^{2}2z+\pi {y}^{2}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{z}^{2}+\pi {y}^{2}z]_{z=-1}^{z=2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4-1)+\pi {y}^{2}(2-(-1))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3+3\pi {y}^{2}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}3+3\pi {y}^{2}\,dy & =[3y+\pi {y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =3(1-0)+\pi (1-0) \\  & =3+\pi \end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Writing a Triple Integral as a Repeated Integral
canonical_examples.problem:
Express the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle 
\iiint\limits_{R} (x+y+z)^2 \: \textrm{d}V
$$

over the box

$$
R = \bigg\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: -1 \leq y \leq 2, \: 0\leq z \leq 2 \bigg\}
$$

as a repeated integral of the form 

$$
\displaystyle 
\int_a^b  \int_c^d  \int_e^f \ldots \: \textrm{d}y\:  \textrm{d}z\:  \textrm{d}x .
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Given the limits for $x,y,$ and $z,$ we can express our triple integral as a repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+y+z)^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(x+y+z)^{2}\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using the Product Rule
canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle 
\iiint\limits_{R} y \cos{x} \sin{z} \: \textrm{d}V
$$

over the box $R = \bigg\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \: 0 \leq z \leq \pi \bigg\}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R = \left[0,\pi/2\right]\times[0,1]\times\left[0,\pi\right]$ is a rectangular box, and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x\,{\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x\,{\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z & =[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi /2}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡z]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (\frac{1}{2}-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R z-xy  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

over the rectangular box $R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \:0 \leq x \leq 2, \: -1 \leq y \leq 1, \: 1 \leq z \leq 3 \right\}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} z-xy \: \textrm{d}V
= 
\int_{-1}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} \int_{1}^{3} z-xy \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}y
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ we write $\textrm d V = \textrm d z\:\textrm d x\:\textrm d y.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}z-xy\,dz\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{3}z-xy\,dz]dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}-xyz]}_{z=1}^{z=3}\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(9-1)-xy(3-1)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}4-2xy\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}4-2xy\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}4-2yx\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[4x-y{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}4(2-0)-y({2}^{2}-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}8-4y\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}8-4y\,dy & =[8y-2{y}^{2}]_{y=-1}^{y=1} \\  & =8(1-(-1))-2({1}^{2}-(-1)^{2}) \\  & =8\cdot 2-2(1-1) \\  & =16-0 \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$
